name: StormHacks
participants_note: 769 registered on Devpost; college students only.

prizes.name: Finalists
prizes.reward: Headphones, a coding-platform subscription and office tours per member
prizes.notes: Top tier of the event; the three finalists are not ranked against each other.

prizes.name: Surge Choice Award
prizes.reward: Smart speaker and an office tour per member
prizes.notes: Chosen by the organizing team for the most creative and inspiring project.

prizes.name: Best Beginner
prizes.notes: At least half the team must be first-time hackers.

prizes.name: Best Game
prizes.reward: Speaker and audio plugin per member

prizes.name: Best Solo Project
prizes.notes: Judged on creativity, technical execution and a complete, polished project without a team.

prizes.name: Most Likely to Become a Startup
prizes.reward: Hosting credits for all; AI credits of USD 5,000 / 3,000 / 2,000 for the top three
prizes.notes: Project pages do not show the order.

prizes.name: Huawei Custom Challenge #1: Interactive Landscape Graphics
prizes.reward: Earbuds, an office tour and a research-team meeting per member
prizes.notes: Real-time ray-marched procedural terrain, from sponsor starter code.

prizes.name: Huawei Custom Challenge #2: Automatic Decision for Re-computation
prizes.reward: Earbuds, an office tour and a research-team meeting per member
prizes.notes: Order a model's operators under a memory limit, with optional recomputation, to minimise compute time.

prizes.name: Safe Software Best Modern C++
prizes.reward: Swag and access to the sponsor's platform
prizes.notes: Judged on modern C++ features, clean interfaces, correctness and safety, and performance.

prizes.name: ColorStack Most Portable Project
prizes.notes: Best designed for on-the-go use: mobile, wearable or AR/VR.

prizes.name: Charles Chang Institute of Entrepreneurship Prize Track
United Nations Sustainable Development Goals Enactus Challenge
prizes.reward: Speakers, battery packs or gift cards per member by rank
prizes.notes: Judged on front end, back end, design, creativity and how well the project addresses a chosen SDG. Project pages do not show the order.

prizes.name: CSSS Rube Goldberg Challenge
prizes.notes: Make a simple task hilariously complex.

prizes.name: Software Systems Prize
prizes.notes: For teams with at least two Software Systems students.

prizes.name: IEEE SFU Prize Track
prizes.notes: Best application of electrical, electronic or computing principles to a real problem.

prizes.name: Best Use of SFU Courses API

prize_count_note: CAD 32,600 in cash plus prizes in kind.

sources.note: Dates, venue, participants, prizes, judging criteria.
All 10 pages captured: 217 of 217 submissions; prize names from each of the 27 winning project pages.

curator_notes: All 27 prize winners are analyzed records. The three Finalists are the top tier and are not ranked; finalists that also won a track prize take the higher-weight track-winner status with both awards listed. The rules page does not state a team size (one winning team has five members), so team_size is null. Taglines are CrafterWIKI paraphrases; domains assigned conservatively.
